idea: A circle with center (h,k) and radius r is (x−h)2+(y−k)2=r2. From x2+y2+Dx+Ey=F, complete the square: add (2D​)2 and (2E​)2 to both sides. Divide out any common coefficient on x2 and y2 first.
trap: Forgetting to add the completing-the-square terms to the right side, or to divide by the coefficient of x2 first.
desmos: Desmos draws the circle, and you can read the center if it lands on grid lines. With a missing coefficient, completing the square is faster and exact.

items.stem: In the xy-plane, the graph of x2+y2+12x−8y=−3 is a circle. What is the radius of the circle?
items.explain: Complete the square: (x+6)2+(y−4)2=−3+36+16=49. The radius is 49​=7.

items.stem: In the xy-plane, the graph of 4x2+4y2+24x+8y=60 is a circle. What is the radius of the circle?

items.stem: In the xy-plane, the graph of x2+y2−8x+by=−48, where b is a constant, is a circle with radius 2. If b<0, what is the y-coordinate of the center of the circle?
items.explain: Complete the square: (x−4)2+(y+2b​)2=−48+16+4b2​. Setting this equal to 4: 4b2​=36, so b=±12; the sign condition gives b=−12. The center's y-coordinate is −2b​=6.
